patients.name: Maria Lopez
patients.scenario: Payer denies the first request; the agent appeals with stronger evidence.

documents.title: Primary care visit
documents.text: Chief complaint: low back pain radiating to the left leg. Symptoms began after lifting boxes and have persisted for 3 months. Pain 7/10, worse with sitting. Exam: positive straight leg raise on the left at 40 degrees. Strength 5/5 bilaterally, reflexes symmetric. Plan: Referred to physical therapy twice weekly. Start naproxen 500 mg twice daily. Return in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Physical therapy discharge summary
documents.text: Diagnosis: lumbar radiculopathy. Patient completed 8 weeks of physical therapy (16 sessions) focused on core stabilization and McKenzie extension exercises. Minimal improvement in radicular pain; pain remains 6/10. Patient adherent to home exercise program. Discharged from therapy due to plateau; recommend physician follow-up for further evaluation.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.text: Follow-up for left L5 radicular pain. Persistent symptoms despite physical therapy and scheduled NSAIDs. New numbness over the dorsum of the left foot. No bowel or bladder changes. No prior imaging of the lumbar spine. Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation and nerve root compression; consider spine referral pending results.

documents.title: Active medications
documents.text: Naproxen 500 mg by mouth twice daily, started 2026-07-14. Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime as needed, started 2026-08-20. Lisinopril 10 mg daily.

patients.name: James Carter

order.diagnosis: M23.91 Unspecified internal derangement of right knee

patients.scenario: Complete request on the first pass; payer approves.

documents.title: Sports medicine visit
documents.text: Right knee pain after a twisting injury playing soccer. Reports episodes of locking and catching of the right knee, and the knee gives way on stairs. Exam: medial joint line tenderness, positive McMurray test. Plan: right knee radiographs, ibuprofen, home exercise program, return in 6 weeks.

documents.title: X-ray right knee, 3 views
documents.text: Radiographs of the right knee, three views: no fracture or dislocation. Joint spaces preserved. Small joint effusion. Impression: no acute osseous abnormality.

documents.title: Sports medicine follow-up
documents.text: Has done the home exercise program and ibuprofen for 6 weeks with persistent mechanical symptoms. Continues to have locking episodes weekly. Plan: MRI right knee without contrast to evaluate for meniscal tear.
